title: Clip a spring-hinged fingertip pulse oximeter onto a patient's index finger while steadying the hand
instruction: Put the pulse oximeter all the way onto the manikin hand's index finger without dragging the hand.
context: Taking vital signs, SpO2 by fingertip pulse oximeter included, is a core duty of nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00: 'Record vital signs, such as temperature, blood pressure, pulse...'; about 1.4 million US jobs, BLS May 2024) and medical assistants (31-9092.00: 'measure their vital signs'; 811,000, BLS 2024), repeated every round of every shift. Errors: the fingertip stops short of the probe's stop, so the light misses the nail bed and the reading fails; the clip goes on the wrong finger or upside down; the patient's limp hand is tugged. The clip has to be squeezed open and kept open while it slides over a fingertip with only 2-3 mm to spare, then let go so its spring clamps. The patient's hand is light and loose on an elevation wedge and slides when pushed, so the other hand steadies it. Unlike #732 (a rigid sleeve; the hard part was deciding how to answer an alarm), this tests the squeeze-slide-release on a working spring clip.
setup: Metres; world x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.750); table top z=0.7475. (1) Arm-elevation wedge, fixed (taped down): firm polyurethane foam, vinyl covered, 250 mm wide (x 0.085..0.335), sloping 20 deg up toward -y: 5 mm thick at its low end (y=0.141), 66.6 mm at its high edge (y=-0.028), 180 mm along the slope, a vertical face below the high edge. (2) Task-trainer adult right hand, free, 0.300 kg, silicone skin over a foam core, palm down on the slope, fingers pointing up the slope (-y): ANSUR-II median size, 193 mm wrist crease to middle fingertip, 86 mm across the knuckles, 26 mm thick palm; index finger 95 mm tip to knuckle, distal 18 mm wide x 15 mm thick, middle 19 x 16, proximal 21 x 18; fingers slightly spread (fingertip centres 36, 68 and 98 mm from the index); thumb beside the index; a 60 x 40 mm forearm stub at the wrist. Its frame origin (0.270,-0.075,0.8312) lies on the slope plane under the index fingertip apex (0.270,-0.0724,0.8382); index, middle and ring tips reach 50 mm past the wedge's high edge. (3) Fingertip pulse oximeter, free, 50 g with two AAA cells (lower body 32 g, upper jaw 18 g), 58 x 32 x 37 mm (ChoiceMMed MD300C-series size): grey lower body 10 mm thick with a silicone finger trough (4 mm flat centre, sides rising at 20 deg to 5 mm at the edges) and a finger stop 34 mm inside the mouth; blue upper jaw 8.5 mm thick with a dark display window, hinged across the body 20 mm from the back end; a 1.5 mm ridged squeeze tab on the last 8 mm of the upper jaw. Jaws parallel with a 17 mm gap at 0 deg; closed stop -20 deg (4 mm gap at the mouth), open stop +25 deg (the back ends meet; the back end is then 31 mm thick). Torsion spring 0.104 N m/rad preloaded to -45 deg: 0.045 N m holding it shut, about 2.3 N on a 16 mm finger, about 8 N squeeze at the tab to open fully. It lies display up on the slope beside the little finger (clip centre x=0.130), its back end overhanging the high edge by 16 mm, mouth pointing down the slope. Friction (static/dynamic): wedge 0.6/0.5, hand 0.5/0.4, oximeter 1.0/0.9. Full collider tables in README.
scoring: Measured on the oximeter and the trainer hand only. Sticky zero for the whole trial: the hand is ever dragged more than 25 mm across the wedge, lifted more than 15 mm or turned more than 15 deg from where it lay (the patient's hand was yanked), or the oximeter ever falls below the table top (off the table). Otherwise every credit needs, held for 1 s: the oximeter ON the index finger: the index fingertip at least 15 mm inside the mouth, with its axis within 12 mm of the clip's centre line between the jaws, pointing in; the upper jaw resting on the finger (jaw angle -10 to +6 deg: not shut empty at -20, not squeezed open); display up (within 45 deg of vertical); the oximeter clear of the table; both grippers released (each gripper centre at least 30 mm from the bounding boxes of the oximeter and of the hand); oximeter and hand at rest (moving under 0.5 mm and 0.25 deg per 50 ms step). That earns 0.4; +0.3 if seated (fingertip within 5 mm of the finger stop); +0.3 if the hand is still on its mark (within 10 mm and 5 deg of where it lay). All three = 1.0. On another finger, upside down, held, still moving or less than 15 mm in = 0. Success = 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial: mark the hand's outline on the wedge; after the robot lets go, photograph from the side and measure with a ruler the fingertip-to-stop gap through the clip's open side, and the hand's shift from its outline; the jaw angle (resting on the finger vs. wide open) and display side are read from the photo.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes 28 s
reset_notes: Lay the hand back on its outline on the wedge, fingers up the slope; put the oximeter back display up beside the little finger with its back end 16 mm past the high edge, jaws shut.
fidelity: The trainer hand is rigid (real ones flex slightly) and built from spheres along each finger and over the palm. The clip's silicone pads are rigid; its jaws clamp by a calibrated torsion spring on one hinge. The oximeter's electronics are not simulated: a seated, clamped clip is what gives a reading. Hand and clip lie on a 20 deg elevation wedge so the robot's wrist can reach behind the clip; a real nurse would also lift the hand.
